Thank you for joining us. This site is to support your learning during this Quantitative Section of the *2026 Howard University ELPS Methods and Data Institute*. My name is [Professor Nathan Alexander](about.qmd){target="_blank"} and I will be today's facilitator.

This workshop is about quantitative data collection and analysis. For this course, I will take a Computational Studies in Education (CSIE) approach. CSIE is an interdisciplinary field that uses computational methods — like data analysis, modeling, and machine learning — to study how people learn, behave, and interact in social and educational contexts. At its core, it blends ideas from education, the social sciences, and computer science.

Instead of relying only on traditional paper-based methods that focus on small-scale surveys or interviews, this field works with large-scale and complex data for:

- Analyzing student performance data from online learning platforms
- Studying social behavior through social media or digital interactions
- Modeling how ideas spread in classrooms or communities

Given our time constraints today, we'll focus on a few key foundations.

## Learning Outcomes

By the end of this workshop, you will be able to:

- Describe basic data analysis workflows using real-world educational data 
- Produce a technical reports using what is called an R Markdown (in Quarto)  
- Import, clean, and visualize data using `tidyverse` tools  
- Formulate and interpret equity-focused research questions using data  
- Extend these methods to support your dissertation research and analysis
